claims.quote: MSK: meniscus / ACL tears, rotator cuff, labrum, AVN of femoral head (early), stress fracture, osteomyelitis.

claims.text: Radiographs first; they may show ⍉abnormalities for months. Earliest findings: localized areas of sclerosis and lucency; later a subchondral crescent sign (frx in the epiphysis) may appear; then gross collapse and flattening of the articular surface, followed by advanced degen chgs
claims.quote: Radiographs should be performed initially (1). They may show no abnormalities for months. The earliest findings are localized areas of sclerosis and lucency. Later, a subchondral crescent sign due to a fracture in the epiphysis may appear. Then, gross collapse and flattening of the articular surface is seen, followed by advanced degenerative changes.

claims.text: When clin sus = ↑ but radiographs are norm or nondiagnostic, MRI (much more sensitive and more specific) should be done early, to ⍉ongoing damage to weight-bearing joints; both hips should be imaged
claims.quote: When clinical suspicion is high but radiographs are normal or nondiagnostic, an MRI, which is much more sensitive and more specific, should be done early in the course of diagnosis to avoid ongoing damage to weight-bearing joints that would limit the success of joint-saving procedures (2). Both hips should be imaged.

claims.text: Labs studies are USU norm but might help detect an underlying dx (eg, coag defects, hemoglobinopathies, lipid abnormalities)
claims.quote: Laboratory studies are usually normal and of little value in detecting osteonecrosis. However, they might help detect an underlying disorder (eg, coagulation defects, hemoglobinopathies, lipid abnormalities).

claims.text: Eti Mech: death of the cellular elements of the bone marrow; nontraumatic mechanisms may incl embolization by blood clots or lipid droplets, intravasc thrombosis and extravasc compress
claims.quote: Osteonecrosis involves the death of cellular elements of the bone marrow. Mechanisms of nontraumatic osteonecrosis may include embolization by blood clots or lipid droplets, intravascular thrombosis, and extravascular compression (1).

claims.text: Osteonecrosis can be idiopathic, caused by trauma or ← nontraumatic factors; the MCC = trauma
claims.quote: Osteonecrosis can be idiopathic, caused by trauma, or due to nontraumatic factors. The most common cause of osteonecrosis is trauma (1, 2).

claims.text: The MCC of traumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head = a displaced subcapital frx of the prox femur
claims.quote: The most common cause of traumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head is a displaced subcapital fracture of the proximal femur; osteonecrosis is uncommon after intertrochanteric fractures.

claims.text: MC nontraumatic factors: glucocorticoid use (particularly w prolonged use and/or higher doses) and excessive EToH consumption; others incl chemo, coag disorders, Cushing syndrome, decompression sickness, hemoglobinopathy (eg, sickle cell dz), HIV infect, organ transplantation, radiation, smoke and SLE
claims.quote: The most common factors causing or contributing to nontraumatic osteonecrosis are (3, 4, 5) Glucocorticoid use (particularly with prolonged use and/or higher doses) Excessive alcohol consumption Other nontraumatic risk factors for osteonecrosis include Chemotherapy Coagulation disorders (eg, antiphospholipid syndrome, inherited thrombophilia, hypofibrinolytic disorders) Cushing syndrome Decompression sickness Dyslipidemia Gaucher disease Hemoglobinopathy (eg, sickle cell disease) HIV infection Liver disease Organ transplantation Pancreatitis Radiation Smoking Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and other inflammatory diseases

claims.text: Nontraumatic osteonecrosis affects men more often than women, primarily b/n ages 30 and 50; @ the hip it = bilat in ≈ 60%
claims.quote: Nontraumatic osteonecrosis affects men more often than women and occurs primarily in patients between ages 30 and 50 years (1). Nontraumatic osteonecrosis of the hip is bilateral in approximately 60% of patients (2).

claims.text: Sx Affected areas may remain aSx for Wks-M after the vasc insult; USU pain then develops gradually, although it may be acute; w progress collapse, pain increases, = exacerbated by motion and wt bearing, and = relieved by rest
claims.quote: Areas affected by osteonecrosis may remain asymptomatic for weeks to months after the vascular insult. Usually pain then develops gradually, although it may be acute. With progressive collapse of the joint, pain increases and is exacerbated by motion and weight bearing and is relieved by rest.

claims.text: Hip: groin pain that may radiate down the thigh or into the buttock; motion becomes limited, and a limp USU develops
claims.quote: Osteonecrosis of the hip causes groin pain that may radiate down the thigh or into the buttock. Motion becomes limited, and a limp usually develops.

claims.text: Sm, aSx lesions, esp those ⍉in weight-bearing areas, may heal spontaneously and may ⍉need tx; Sxtomatic or medium-sized or greater lesions are often treated (eg, core decompression) to improve the chance of heal w.o joint collapse; contributing factors should be mitigated (eg, limiting corticosteroid use)
claims.quote: Small, asymptomatic lesions, especially those not in weight-bearing areas, may heal spontaneously and may not need treatment. However, lesions that are symptomatic or medium-sized or greater are often treated (for example, with a simple procedure such as core decompression) to improve the chance that lesions heal without joint collapse (1). With or without other treatment, contributing factors should be mitigated (eg, limiting corticosteroid use) to promote healing of the lesion.

claims.text: Surg = most effective b4 joint collapse; core decompression, the procedure most frequently done, drills one or more sm tracks into the osteonecrotic area to decrease intraosseous P and stim repair
claims.quote: Surgical treatments for osteonecrosis are most effective when performed before joint collapse. They have been used most often in treating osteonecrosis of the femoral head where the prognosis without treatment is worse than that for osteonecrosis in other regions. Core decompression is the procedure most frequently done; a drill is used to make 1 or more small tracks or perforations in the osteonecrotic area in an attempt to decrease intraosseous pressure and stimulate repair by ingrowth of progenitor cells.

claims.text: If extensive collapse of the femoral head and degen chgs in the acetabulum cause sig pain and funct impairment, total hip arthroplasty = the most reliable intervention
claims.quote: If extensive collapse of the femoral head and degenerative changes in the acetabulum cause significant pain and functional impairment, total hip arthroplasty is the most reliable intervention for pain relief and functional restoration (8).
